title: Jazz band gigs as a message of love
summary: Pierce-Capp and Bill Berry band jobs pay little and are done for love of jazz by studio players.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: How about jobs like I saw you play last Sunday (inaudible)?

Those type of jobs are more a message of love. There's very little money attached to it and most of those jobs are performed by people that just want to play certain types of music and get together and enjoy themselves and still carry on the idiom of jazz.
We're talking at this point about Nat Pierce (PHONETIC), Frankie (inaudible).

Talking about the Nat Pierce, Frankie Catt Juggernaut Bank (PHONETIC). The same thing goes for the Bill Barry Orchestra and all of those types that get into the playing of jazz because most of those jobs are performed by

people that have stabilized themselves with very nice jobs and this is just a side thing to them. Most of those guys work in the studios and make commercials and are in a good category of living and this thing -- those type of jobs, working in bands (inaudible), whatever the name of that -- is that --
They changed the name of the Pilgrimage Theater to the John Anson (PHONETIC) Four.

The John Anson Ford, Pilgrimage and all those other things that are played for the musical performers -- and such things as that. They just about pay for your gas money and the cost of your parking of your meal away from home, to play one of them. There is actually no money made hardly on those type of jobs. It's a message of love to work them.
